_comment: SSOT for Claude hook installation. Read by lib/sync/core.sh (which files to
symlink into $CONFIG_DIR/hooks) and by lib/common.sh:ensure_rules_enforcement_hooks
(which entries to reconcile into settings.json).
Before this file existed the two lists were maintained separately, so a hook
could be installed as a file and never wired into settings.json — it then sat
in the hooks dir as silent dead code. Adding a hook now means adding one entry
here; anything not listed is neither linked nor registered.
Fields: event = Claude Code hook event; matcher = tool-name regex or null for
events that take no matcher; script = basename inside runtimes/claude/hooks/.
Order is the order entries are appended to a fresh settings.json.
'run' is optional: a command template where {path} expands to the installed
hook path. Omit it and the command is `node "{path}"`, which is what every JS
hook wants. It exists because a bash hook, an env prefix, or a subcommand
argument cannot be expressed by the node default — the compact-gate entries
need all three. Note the matcher for PreCompact/PostCompact is matched against
the compaction `trigger`, and for SessionEnd against `reason`, not a tool name.
'settings' holds top-level settings.json keys the hooks depend on. A hook
can be registered perfectly and still be inert if the runtime option it was
sized against is missing — the compact gate's 800k ceiling only makes sense
above a 700k compaction point, and with autoCompactWindow left at Claude's
default the ceiling sits above every reachable token count, so the gate
registers, fires, and defers against a window it was never tuned for. These
keys are reconciled like the hooks: the manifest owns them and sync sets
them, so the pairing cannot drift apart across machines.
'retired' lists hooks this repo used to ship. Ownership is decided by asking
whether the repo has the file, so a hook deleted outright stops looking like
ours and its settings.json entry would linger forever. Naming it here keeps it
prunable. Entries can be dropped once every machine has synced past them.

hooks.enforces: denies .agents destinations for Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and oversized non-generated writes from observable tool input; Bash is guarded only by payload size because shell path semantics are not inferred
closes the oversized heredoc/tee/echo bypass of pre-edit-gate

attaches scoped serena find_symbol(kind + one-based body span) beside an rg/grep single-symbol definition lookup without denying the original search; emits tool_use_id-keyed opportunity, attempt, terminal, delivery, and consumption evidence. The systemd project-server is the sole port owner; warm scoped queries measured about 255ms on boltz-red.

on exactly the third distinct repository-contained source destination in a current assistant turn, queries the existing Graphify graph and code-review-graph's read-only worktree impact, then attaches bounded tool_use_id-keyed context.
token efficiency; staged by on-disk size, bounded reads pass

10-context 압축 게이트 — defers auto-compaction to a work-unit boundary; exit 2 blocks, every failure path allows. One entry, not one per trigger: the manifest contract is one registration per script, and the script itself allows immediately when trigger is manual

appends one behavioural row per SessionEnd (NOT per session: exit/clear/logout/prompt_input_exit/resume each fire it, and each firing rescans the whole transcript, so one session's rows are cumulative snapshots — consumers must group by `session` before summing, or the same call is counted once per ending; measured 72 rows over 50 sessions, +217% rg and +250% serena) to ~/.claude/uptake/rows.jsonl. The full ~/.claude/projects scan is not slow (measured 2026-08-14: 6.8s over 10,675 files) — it simply only ran when someone remembered it, the same failure mode every measurement here keeps finding. Incremental (0.3s/session), and carries the counters that answer whether symbol-search-gate works: nav.serena against its 0.9% baseline, and gate.escape as the false-positive alarm
clears a busy marker the session forgot to release; no matcher, so it covers exit/clear/logout/prompt_input_exit
